claims.text: Increasing phosphorus content by approximately 5–10 at.% will improve glass-forming ability relative to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Increasing phosphorus content by approximately 5–10 at.% will improve the thermal stability of the amorphous state relative to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 can form an amorphous structure under very rapid cooling by melt-spinning.
Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 develops a complex multiphase crystalline microstructure under slower cooling.
The proposed intervention is to change the nominal composition from Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 to Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P25–P30.
The relevant melt-spinning cooling rate is approximately 10^5–10^6 K/s.
Phosphorus enhances glass formation in this alloy system during extremely rapid cooling.
Slower cooling promotes formation of multiple crystalline phases in Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20.
Increasing phosphorus concentration will promote short-range-ordered, phosphide-rich regions.
Phosphide-rich short-range order will interfere with long-range atomic rearrangements and inhibit crystallization.
Additional phosphorus will disrupt the atomic ordering required for crystalline nucleation and growth.
Disruption of crystalline ordering will slow crystallization kinetics.
Slower crystallization kinetics will extend the undercooling range and stabilize the amorphous structure.
The phosphorus-enriched alloy will have a higher amorphous fraction than Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 under identical rapid-quenching conditions.
The phosphorus-enriched alloy will exhibit shifted crystallization temperatures corresponding to a broader thermal-stability window.
The benefit of additional phosphorus will occur predominantly at extremely high cooling rates and may disappear at lower cooling rates.
Increased phosphorus may reduce alloy ductility.

contradictions.description: The stated compositions are labeled as atomic percentages but Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P25 and Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P30 sum to 105 and 110, respectively. If normalized, they contain about 23.81 and 27.27 at.% P, only about 3.81 and 7.27 percentage points above the 20 at.% baseline rather than the stated 5–10 at.% increase.
